title: 13: Redis Insight Developer Workflow
subtitle: 15-step Redis Insight UI walkthrough covering Browser, key filtering/editing, Workbench, CLI, Search, Analyze, and Pub/Sub.

steps.title: Open the Redis Browser
steps.why: Start in Redis Insight Browser to inspect keys and their data types in the connected Local Redis database.

steps.title: Select the user:1001 hash key
steps.why: Select a real hash key so the detail pane shows its fields, TTL, size, and current values.

steps.title: Search for user keys
steps.why: Use the Browser key search field to narrow the key list to names containing the user prefix.

steps.title: Filter the Browser to HASH keys
steps.why: Use the type filter to show only hash data structures while keeping the user search active.

steps.title: Update a field in the selected hash
steps.why: Modify the selected user hash by adding a status field, demonstrating Redis hash editing in the Browser detail workflow.

steps.title: Open Workbench
steps.why: Switch to Redis Insight Workbench, the command-oriented workspace used to compose and run Redis commands.

steps.title: Enter a HGETALL command
steps.why: Place a Redis command in the Workbench editor so the selected user hash can be inspected from the command layer.

steps.title: Run the Workbench command
steps.why: Execute the Workbench query and display a command result, testing the Run control and result surface.

steps.title: Open the built-in Redis CLI
steps.why: Expand Redis Insight's CLI panel to test the persistent command-line surface inside the same application.

steps.title: Run DBSIZE in the CLI
steps.why: Execute DBSIZE from the built-in CLI and verify that command history and output remain visible in the CLI panel.

steps.title: Open the Search workspace
steps.why: Switch to the Redis Search workspace and focus the idx:products search index.

steps.title: Run a product search query
steps.why: Execute a Redis Search query for keyboard products in a price range and show the result table.

steps.title: Inspect the Slow Log
steps.why: Open Analyze and switch to Slow Log so command duration and client activity can be inspected.

steps.title: Start the Redis profiler
steps.why: Open the Profiler analysis surface and start profiling to demonstrate Redis command monitoring state.

steps.title: Publish a Pub/Sub test message
steps.why: Finish the UI test in Pub/Sub by publishing a message and showing it in the live message stream.
